reason: Signing, the updater and publishing really are unbuilt: tauri.conf.json has no signing keys and createUpdaterArtifacts:false (:45), build.yml runs `pnpm tauri build` labelled '(unsigned)' (:76-77) and only uploads CI artifacts (:79-84), with no Releases publish step and no Homebrew cask. Two details are wrong. (a) AppImage and .deb ARE built: tauri.conf.json:32 lists targets deb/appimage/nsis/app/dmg and the ubuntu matrix leg of build.yml builds and uploads them; what is missing is signing and publishing, not the Linux build. (b) Per BLOCKERS.md:305-307 the landing page lives in a separate operator-owned private repo, so its absence from this repo proves nothing; the real evidence is that terminal.vysted.com returns NXDOMAIN, so it is not deployed. Severity stays high for a public 0.9.0: unsigned binaries plus no updater path means users cannot install cleanly and cannot receive fixes.
evidence_checked: Opened tauri.conf.json and all three workflows. Grepped the workflows for signing, release, cache, Homebrew and AppImage. Read BLOCKERS.md launch-ops items 1-7. Ran a DNS lookup and a curl against terminal.vysted.com.
repro_check: grep -n 'SignPath|TAURI_SIGNING|APPLE_CERT|release' .github/workflows/*.yml -> only the artifact path at build.yml:83; `host terminal.vysted.com` -> NXDOMAIN; tauri.conf.json:32 targets include deb+appimage (built, unsigned, not published).

The mechanism it depends on (dragDropEnabled:false at tauri.conf.json:23) is present, and the missing piece is verification, not a failing core flow. reason: Confirmed end to end. The catalog advertises an optional `highlight` arg to 'spotlight' a metric (catalog.py:997-1013). host-actions.ts:1078-1079 reads it and passes it to openCompanyOverview, which stores it in useEquityCommandStore (host-actions.ts:284, equity-command.ts:31-33). The only consumer, EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:822-833, reads only `equityCommand.symbol`, and nothing under src/modules/ reads `highlightMetric`. It is worse than silent: the host-action result string (host-actions.ts:1080-1081, 'spotlighting <metric>') and the proposal preview (host-actions.ts:690-699, '<metric> spotlighted') both tell the user and the model that a highlight happened when none did.
evidence_checked: Read every cited line. Grepped src, types and sidecar for highlightMetric and highlight_metric: the hits were only host-actions.ts and equity-command.ts, with no reader in the modules.
repro_check: grep -rn highlightMetric src --include=*.tsx -> no hits in any panel; the consumer effect at EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:822-833 uses only equityCommand.symbol.

reason: The dead field is real. WorkflowRunRequest declares mode and resume_from (models/workflow.py:73-74), mirrored in types/workflow.ts:83-89, but run_workflow calls workflow_engine.run_workflow(payload.spec, inputs=payload.inputs, ...) and never reads either field (routers/workflow.py:39-56). A resume-from request therefore silently runs the full graph. I corrected the severity to low. The only in-product caller hard-codes mode:'full' (NodeEditorPanel.tsx:389), and the MCP run_workflow tool takes only spec_json (MCP_INTEGRATION.md:128), so no user flow can send resume-from. Only a hand-written REST caller would hit it. The smallest fix stays the same: 400 on an unimplemented mode, or delete the field from both mirrors.
evidence_checked: Read the model, the router and the TS mirror. Grepped src, types and sidecar for resume-from, resumeFrom and resume_from (declarations only) and for /workflow/run callers (only NodeEditorPanel, which sends mode 'full'). I did not POST, because a non-GET goes only through vy.py and the code path settles the claim.
repro_check: grep -rn 'resume_from|resumeFrom' sidecar src types -> only the model and type declarations; NodeEditorPanel.tsx:389 body = {spec, mode: 'full'}.

reason: It is true that no artifact proves Claude Desktop consuming Vysted through mcp-remote; r9/claude-desktop-full.png sits among design-reference captures (claude-composer, cursor-*, linear-web) and is not proof. The 'why it matters' is overstated, though. The protocol interop the finding says was never demonstrated has been proven live: the code/mcp-servers census drove a real `POST /mcp/ initialize` on :52152 and got a full capability handshake, and GET /mcp/status on :52152 returns ready:true with toolCount:36. A stdio transport also exists (MCP_INTEGRATION.md:77-99), so mcp-remote is not the only route for Claude Desktop. What is left is the lack of a client-specific end-to-end demo, which is low. Separately, the doc's claim at MCP_INTEGRATION.md:155-156 that tools appear in Claude Desktop's slash-command picker as `/vysted__price_data` likely describes the UI inaccurately and deserves a check during that demo.
evidence_checked: Read the MCP_INTEGRATION.md HTTP, stdio and Claude Desktop sections. Listed the r9 references dir. Read the prior census's live initialize-handshake evidence. Ran GET /mcp/status against :52152. I did not open Claude Desktop (no GUI lane).
repro_check: curl -s 127.0.0.1:52152/mcp/status -> {"ready":true,"toolCount":36,"endpoint":"/mcp","protocolVersion":"2025-06-18"}; the Claude Desktop demo itself is NEEDS-GUI.

reason: It is correct that Brave and Mojeek are covered only by an inline HTML fixture (test_brave_backend.py:19,67) and that no scheduled workflow re-validates live markup (no schedule or cron in .github/workflows). The consequence is overstated: markup drift does not by itself make the default tier return zero results. DDG is the primary engine (keyless.py:53 ENGINE_CHAIN = ddg, brave, mojeek), and a zero-row parse rotates to the next engine (keyless.py:170-176). brave.py:8-13 also uses layered selectors so class drift degrades fields before rows. The real mechanism is narrower but still silent. A drifted parser returns an empty SUCCESS, which calls breaker.record_success() (keyless.py:163) and is logged only as 'no results'. The breaker never benches it and tier_status stays healthy, so the fallback is dead exactly in the DDG-throttled case it exists for. The same fixture-only gap applies to the primary DDG parser.
evidence_checked: Read the keyless rotation loop, the brave.py parse contract and the brave test fixtures. Listed the search tests and grepped the workflows for schedule and cron. I made no live SERP fetch (WebSearch budget rules; it is not needed to settle the mechanism).
repro_check: Code-path: brave._parse(drifted html) -> [] -> keyless.py:163 record_success, :175 'no results', continue -> DDG answer is returned if DDG is up; if DDG is throttled -> empty 'found nothing' at :186-189 instead of an error.
